# Quantitative HCI Liquid Glass

> Agent-first behaviours, visual components and design tools built on Vercel UI SDK. React rendering; @ui-sdk/core and @ui-sdk/react pinned to 0.1.0-beta.13. Custom work remains Unvalidated by a human UI/UX team.

This is a private React workspace package, not a published npm release. Use the checked-out workspace and locked dependencies. Preserve existing application state and the shared material.

## Start here

- [Engineering guide](agent-engineering.md): choose, compose, extend, operate and verify.
- [Package guide](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/README.md): provider, material and component recipes.
- [Package instructions](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/AGENTS.md): requirements for future package changes.
- [Compact component index](/agent-index.json): choose by purpose, kind and public export; follow its `contract` URL for one complete entry.
- [Agent contracts](/agent-contracts.json): public export inventory, inputs, state, discovery, actions, restrictions and evidence.
- [Contract schema](/agent-contracts.schema.json): the versioned machine-readable contract format.
- [Custom action inputs](/agent-action-inputs.json): exact JSON argument shapes and examples for both custom primitives. Validate the shape before dispatch; inspect live state for revisions, valid IDs and host acceptance.
- [Release identity](/agent-release.json): package version, source provenance, content fingerprints and all emitted agent documents. Compare the page's `quantive-agent-contract-set` meta value with `release.contractSet` before using cached contracts.

- [Component and recipe registry](/registry/components.json): all SDK families, custom components and compiled composition recipes. This documentation does not provide another action endpoint.

## Choose a component

- [Interactions and Sections](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/docs/hci/standards/interaction-sections.md): scoped effects, real context menus, semantic sections and cancellable chapter selection.
- [Models and transactions](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/src/modeling/README.md): inspect, preview, revision-checked edits, controlled acceptance and history.
- [Agent tasks](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/src/agents/README.md): capabilities, timeline, tool review, context and artifacts; local component schema, not protocol transport.
- [Graphics](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/src/graphics/README.md): layers, transforms, exports and host-owned image requests.
- [Package guide: Standards, shared canvas and images](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/README.md): composition and appearance APIs.
- [Modeling architecture](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/docs/hci/standards/agent-first-modeling.md): shared document, UWE/C4 scope and evaluation.
- [Engineering standard](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/docs/hci/standards/agent-engineering.md): required evidence and future additions.

## Installed upstream authority

Read node_modules/@ui-sdk/core/skills/ui-sdk/SKILL.md and node_modules/@ui-sdk/react/docs/llms.txt first. Open only the needed component, rendering, agent and testing pages. Use installed declaration files to resolve exact types. Import SDK controls directly from @ui-sdk/react/<component>; never @ui-sdk/core/internal/*.

For a local checkout, the registry and schema sit at packages/liquid-glass/agent-contracts.json and packages/liquid-glass/agent-contracts.schema.json. Their hosted copies are served at the root paths above. Resolve source/docs/evidence paths in registry entries from the repository root, not from the hosted URL.

Read only the contract needed: `npm run glass:contract -- --search viewport`, then `npm run glass:contract -- liquid-viewport`. Hosted consumers can fetch `/contracts/liquid-viewport.json`. The full registry is available for tooling; it need not be loaded into every agent conversation.

Preflight custom action arguments without operating a UI: `npm run glass:contract -- validate liquid-viewport panBy '[80,-40]'`. The canonical entry's `runtime.actionSchema` is relative to the package directory. Hosted index entries and contract envelopes expose a separate root-relative `actionSchema` URL so it resolves correctly from `/contracts/<id>.json`. Schema-valid inputs can still be refused by current state, revision checks, permissions or the controlled host. SDK aliases continue to use the installed upstream documentation and live action discovery.

The compact index and individual contract envelopes link their own schemas. Each index entry carries the SHA-256 digest and UTF-8 byte length of its complete contract file. The release metadata lists the other emitted document files and their fingerprints. These are consistency checks, not authenticity signatures, browser test results or human approval. A dirty build reports its base commit without claiming a clean source tree.

The runtime is createAgent from @ui-sdk/react/agent: snapshot, query, act and subscribe. Contracts describe intended use; only executed tests establish that the described behaviour works. See the engineering guide for observable postconditions and limitations.

For model edits, distinguish `requested`, `applied`, `rejected`, `unchanged` and `applied-error`. A resolved host Promise is not acceptance: accepted document props are authoritative, including equivalent serialized copies. Inspect `pendingRevision`, use `cancelPending` to abandon an unpublished proposal, and pass the callback's AbortSignal to asynchronous host work. A failure after an applied change does not roll that change back.

## Composition layers

1. Import genuine controls directly from @ui-sdk/react/<component>.
2. Mount the existing LiquidGlassProvider from @quantitative-hci/liquid-glass/webgpu and kit.css at the app boundary. Reuse the provider when the app already has one. Supply the decorative backdrop deliberately: glass does not capture arbitrary application content.
3. Add @quantitative-hci/liquid-glass/interactions with interactions.css around the intended region. Add @quantitative-hci/liquid-glass/sections with sections.css around meaningful page content.
4. Keep one createAgent bridge from @ui-sdk/react/agent, with the host application's authorization policy. Use the SDK's snapshot, query, act and subscribe; discover fresh refs and current choices before acting. Observe the rendered state after an action, including a cancelled change.

## Interactions

- LiquidCursor({ children, variant: "glass" | "precision" | "native", disabled? }) scopes decoration. Glass uses a precise pointer dot and damped accent; precision follows directly. data-cursor-label supplies a short hint; data-cursor-media identifies a media region; data-cursor="native" explicitly preserves native behavior. Text entry, editable regions, canvas, disabled/pending controls and open native popups retain their native pointer. Keyboard input hides the decoration. The cursor respects effective motion and forced colours and never intercepts events.
- LiquidClickFeedback({ children, effect: "ripple" | "spark" | "none" }) adds a finite, bounded response around real activations. It changes no application state. Do not infer completion of asynchronous work from a press effect; display the actual SDK pending/error state.
- LiquidMagnetic({ children, distance? }) is for an aria-hidden decorative icon inside a genuine control. The label and hit target stay fixed. Never put another control or essential text inside it.
- LiquidContextMenu({ label, triggerLabel?, children, actions, onAction }) composes MenuContextTrigger, MenuTrigger, MenuContent and MenuItem. Actions are { id, label, disabled?, destructive?, requiresConfirmation? }. Keep meaningful, unique IDs and labels. Preserve the visible trigger for discovery and touch; right-click is scoped to the region. Return asynchronous work from onAction so the SDK tracks pending/errors. Keep confirmation on the consequential item, not on opening or cancelling. Host callbacks still own authorization.

Examples: docs/hci/examples/liquid-glass/src/recipes/cursor-feedback.tsx and context-actions.tsx. These examples are included in the TypeScript build and offered through Copy example in the demo.

## Sections

- LiquidSection({ title, eyebrow?, introduction?, actions?, headingLevel?, children }) supplies semantic section and heading structure. Supply real task content and actual SDK actions.
- LiquidShowcaseSection adds media, mediaCaption and layout: "split" | "immersive". Media needs a truthful description/caption and an appropriate accessible alternative.
- LiquidChapterSection({ title, chapters, value?, defaultValue?, onValueChange?, navigationLabel?, followScroll? }) keeps all chapter text readable and the selected media visible. Chapters are { id, label, title, content, media, mediaCaption }. IDs and labels must be unique. The SDK segmented control uses the same controlled value as scroll-following. onValueChange receives { source, reason: "selection" | "scroll", cancel }. Keep cancelled changes from updating the application state. Set followScroll=false for applications that own navigation elsewhere.
- LiquidSectionContour({ variant: "wave" | "ridge" | "orbit", edge? }) is decorative SVG, hidden from assistive technology. It is not a diagram or an information-bearing connection.
- LiquidReveal({ children, once? }) progressively adds a finite opacity response. Content remains present without JavaScript animation or when motion is reduced.

Examples: docs/hci/examples/liquid-glass/src/recipes/showcase-section.tsx and chapter-story.tsx. All four examples include a standalone provider; compose the inner content into an existing provider when integrating with an established app. They intentionally do not initialize another agent bridge: reuse the host's single bridge described above, or initialize it once at the application boundary.

## State, preferences and review

Use meaningful accessible names and real UI SDK callbacks. Do not synthesize clicks to operate an agent-facing state model or expose a second mutation API. Decorative cursor/click/contour/reveal elements have no agent actions. Keep disabled controls disabled for all input routes. Respect data-agent-secret, data-agent-hidden and data-agent-confirm; the demo refuses actions requiring a person.

Honor reduced motion, forced colours, touch input and the selected material. Avoid endless animation, wheel interception, shifting hit targets and cursor replacement over native controls. Suspend effects when the document or collection is hidden and remove observers/listeners during cleanup.

All custom components remain Unvalidated until a recorded human UI/UX team review changes their status. SDK foundation identifies upstream behavior provenance only. Typechecking and browser checks do not establish improved human usability or WCAG conformance.

## Verification

Run npm run glass:verify and the repository's Python browser contract against the production build. Preserve all baseline scenarios and include interactions_pointer_keyboard_agent_and_preferences plus sections_chapters_navigation_and_preferences. Use the existing CI environment for software-WebGPU evidence. Record exact commands, source commit, browser, viewport, failed paths and limitations.

## Sources and reuse

The new React compositions adapt interaction vocabulary from CK.com and Wayrest: scoped cursor modes, fixed hit targets, decorative contours and natural scroll progress. References include https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/menu, https://magicui.design/docs/components/pointer and https://21st.dev/@automate_flows/components/liquid-glass-wordmark-footer. See docs/hci/standards/interaction-sections.md for precise provenance and scope. No premium Motion Cursor or redistribution-restricted React Bits source is included.
